mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the potential economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in real GDP by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a contraction in economic activity, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 drops and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in industrial production by more than 2% month-over-month signals a surge in supply-side activity, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth prospects improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts by more than 5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as broader economic activity is stimulated.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% MoM for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a low federal funds rate (below 1%) signals accommodative monetary policy, which typically supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as cheap borrowing costs fuel economic growth and investment.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances with FEDFUNDS < 1%, or the correlation between low FEDFUNDS and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a strengthening labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending power increases.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases & UNRATE decreases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint correlation between PAYEMS increases, UNRATE decreases, and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism where a significant increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 2% month-over-month during a period of low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2%) signals robust consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between RSAFS increases during low CPIAUCSL and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
